release_content_gate.$comment: Hard release gate for material that must not ship in an App Store archive. Unlike offline_closure (a non-fatal audit of runtime offline invariants), a finding here fails the release assertion. The gate inspects nested ZIP archives because runtime content such as the Pyodide python_stdlib.zip is opaque to a flat file walk. This policy file lives in tools/ and is not copied into the application bundle; it must stay out of any scanned root so that the marker literals below cannot themselves become artifact hits.

forbidden_markers.reason: CPython documents the itms-services URL scheme as an App Store review compatibility issue and removes that handling when built for iOS, so a generic Pyodide Python standard library must be sanitized by the canonical runtime producer before publication

nested_archives.$comment: Scanner mechanics for the release content gate (depth and size limits). Distinct from the top-level nested_archives section, which is the approved-archive allowlist used by bundle hygiene.

bundle_hygiene.$comment: Closed-world structural contract for the final application bundle: deny unknown structure rather than enumerating bad strings. Cruft rules are scoped away from WebPayload because canonical runtime content is governed by the canonical payload contract and the release content gate. Patterns are path-aware: JavaScript, Python, WASM, and wheels inside WebPayload are legitimate and are never banned by extension.

nested_archives.$comment: Unknown nested archives are a way for cruft or unexpected code to bypass ordinary inventory inspection, so every archive must be explicitly approved. An approved archive that cannot be inspected fails closed.

allowed.purpose: canonical runtime Python standard library (producer-owned; sanitization is FortWeb-owned)

executable_inventory.$comment: Only intended native code may ship. Pyodide WebAssembly is runtime content under canonical payload closure, not native code, and is intentionally not listed here.

codesign.$comment: Report-only by default because the CI archive lane builds with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO (unsigned). Promote to "required" once a signed distribution archive is produced; per-item verification already runs and is recorded in the bill of materials.

entitlements.$comment: Capability contract for the signed distribution build. The allowlist below is deliberately limited to profile-issued standard keys; any capability (push, iCloud, app groups, associated domains, network extensions) must be added here deliberately when the project intends it.

secret_material.$comment: High-confidence rules only. No generic entropy scanning: minified runtime JavaScript and WASM would produce constant false positives. embedded.mobileprovision is a platform artifact inspected by signing validation, not accidental secret material.

size_budgets.$comment: Ceilings sized from intended production structure with headroom (historical bundle: ~22 MB, 176 files, 1 nested archive, largest file ~9.6 MB). They must catch an accidentally copied dependency or test tree, not harmless compiler-size drift.

submission_metadata.$comment: What the app declares to iOS/Apple versus what it ships. Structure and reason-code values are taken from Apple's current documentation (privacy manifest files; describing use of required reason API). Hard failures cover structural faults and undeclared capabilities; advisories cover classifications that need owner intent (stale declarations, missing export-compliance declaration).

required_reason_scan.$comment: Static pattern scan of first-party native sources. Observed categories must be declared in the manifest; declared categories with no observed use are reported as stale for owner review rather than silently removed.

info_plist.$comment: Closed-world capability contract. The product currently declares none of these capabilities, so each allowlist is empty on purpose; adding an entry is an explicit product decision.

third_party_sdks.$comment: Apple requires a privacy manifest and (for binary dependencies) a signature for the SDKs listed in "Upcoming third-party SDK requirements". This project links no third-party native SDKs: the Xcode project declares no package references and the archived app contains a single Mach-O executable. The Pyodide Python wheels are runtime payload content under canonical payload closure, not native SDK frameworks.

export_compliance.$comment: Evidence only. Fort-ios ships cryptographic functionality (KERI cryptography and system TLS), so this records what is bundled for a human to answer Apple's export-compliance determination. This file must never be treated as a legal determination.

crypto_components.purpose: KERI key events, CESR signing/verification, pre-rotation
